statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail stays low because equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z and no live NQ price path exists, while Stress holds elevated after a weekend that hardened the US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz against a backdrop of two-decade-high Treasury yields.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. A narrow danger window is published from the Sunday 22:00Z CME equity index futures reopen into the early Asian hours, where the unpriced weekend escalation would first be expressed in price. Existing-position management and emergency protection logic are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 Tail low with futures closed; Stress elevated as Iran warns of a possible US attack after the rejected Hormuz deal
body: Equity index futures have been closed since Friday 21:00Z, so no live NQ price path exists at this assessment time and the current Tail reading reflects absent path risk rather than an observed benign trend. Friday's verified cash close was orderly: the Nasdaq-100 finished at 30,608.14, up 0.42%, mid-range inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 day range and about half a percent below its 30,770.63 52-week high, with the Nasdaq Composite at 27,068.72, the S&P 500 at 7,743.41, the Dow at 51,828.62 and VIX down 5.11% to 14.87. That combination shows no shallow-pullback extension, no holding of session extremes and no volatility stress, so the amplifiers this contract requires before Tail reaches the elevated band are absent. The weekend nevertheless hardened the backdrop. Saturday's rejection of Iran's seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz was followed on Sunday morning by an Iranian army spokesman warning that the United States may launch a military attack and stating the army is fully prepared, with Tehran saying it awaits an official US answer through mediators. Physical disruption is unchanged and extreme, with roughly one Hormuz transit recorded on 20 September against an 85-per-day pre-crisis baseline and about 199 AIS-visible vessels holding off berth. Brent at $104.32 eased 2.1% on Friday on deal optimism that has since been withdrawn, yet remains roughly 20% higher on the month. Rates add a second independent strain: the latest H.15 observation puts the 10-year at 5.18% and the 2-year at 4.87%, near two-decade highs, with commentary pointing to possible October and December hikes. Under this contract that catalyst stack raises Stress and shapes Confidence; it does not by itself establish the pathological price path Tail measures. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and is both stale, at roughly 111 minutes, and partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so its latest-session breadth and megacap figures were treated strictly as delayed supporting context and were not used as evidence of current NQ structure. Those internals read uneven rather than uniformly aligned. The published danger window covers the 22:00Z CME reopen into the early Asian hours, which is the first venue where the weekend developments can be priced.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots are available from published Claude assessments and were left unchanged. Tail drifted from 8 down to 6 before ticking back to 7, Stress rose from 47 to 62 and Confidence decayed from 82 to 68 across the period, reflecting an orderly Friday cash session followed by a weekend with no live price discovery and an increasingly demanding rates, oil and geopolitical backdrop. The mapped state remained EA_ON throughout, and the dominant mode stayed normal because no slot in the window contained observable one-way structure.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail in the low band across all 24 hours. Risk is held near the closed-period baseline through the remainder of Sunday, lifts into a published danger window at the 22:00Z CME equity index futures reopen where the unpriced weekend Hormuz rejection and the Iranian military warnings would first be expressed in price, and then decays through the Asian hours on the base assumption that reopen pricing is absorbed with normal two-way discovery. Confidence falls slightly while the evidence set ages without refreshing observation, then recovers once a live NQ price path exists again after 22:00Z. Every value after the current clock-hour is conditional: no post-reopen gap, continuation or retracement has been observed, and the next hourly assessments will re-score these hours against actual price-path evidence.
